assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and credit-cycle amplification are a foundational mechanism in macroeconomics. The Kiyotaki-Moore framework and the financial-accelerator literature shaped the modern analysis of financial frictions, crisis dynamics and central-bank policy. The influence on both theory and policy practice is very broad.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) is the clearest theoretical origin of credit cycles driven by collateral values. Gertler's work on financial frictions, with Bernanke and Gilchrist on the accelerator and with Kiyotaki on intermediation, extends the programme. Gilchrist is a meaningful contributor but is left out because of the three-laureate limit. Bernanke's earlier prize was for banking crises, so there is some overlap in the field.
assessment.maturity: Core contributions are about thirty years old and have been tested by the 2008 crisis and by later work on financial intermediation. The prize would not be premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to credit the accelerator with Gilchrist over Gertler
Overlap with the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises
Empirical evidence on the strength of the mechanisms is mixed and model-dependent

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The structural estimation of differentiated-product demand and dynamic industry models transformed empirical industrial organisation. The methods are standard in merger analysis, antitrust and regulation, and they spread to trade, health and environmental economics.
assessment.attribution: Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes (1995) is the canonical contribution, and Berry (1994) is its identification precursor. Pakes is also credited with the dynamic-oligopoly framework and with the estimation theory. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin are important but are excluded by the three-name limit. The line between the individual contributions is clear enough for a trio.
assessment.maturity: Developed over thirty years with extensive practical use and replication. It is well confirmed as a method.
uncertainties: The longlist has seven names, so the cut of three involves a judgment about Bresnahan and Reiss
The field's results depend on structural modelling assumptions
My own expertise in industrial organisation should not count as evidence of merit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mian and Sufi showed with granular data that household leverage and credit supply expansions drove the housing boom, the bust and the depth of the recession. This changed how macroeconomists and policymakers think about credit cycles, and the work moves between micro evidence and macro implications.
assessment.attribution: The two are consistently joint authors of the central papers and book. Campbell is a major finance scholar, but his work on household debt is less central to this discovery, so a two-name award is cleaner.
assessment.maturity: The main work is from about 2009 to 2018, so it is relatively recent but widely replicated and influential. A prize is plausible now but it could also wait.
uncertainties: Debate over the quantitative size of the credit-supply channel versus other explanations
Debate over the relative contributions of demand and supply factors
Less time for the work to be tested across episodes than for older candidates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the measurement of trade shocks reshaped understanding of wage inequality, polarization and the local effects of globalization. The empirical findings influenced both research and public policy debate.
assessment.attribution: Autor and Katz span the skill-biased and task-based work. Hanson, Dorn and Autor carry the China-shock papers. The longlist caps credit at three names, which forces a choice between the technology and the trade strands, and the award would be somewhat split. Acemoglu's prize overlaps partly on tasks.
assessment.maturity: Contributions date from the 1990s to the 2010s, and the China-shock findings have been extensively debated and refined. It is mature enough for an award.
uncertainties: Contested interpretation and identification in the China-shock literature
How to credit Dorn and Autor-Levy-Murnane, who sit outside this credit list
Overlap with the 2023 and 2024 prizes

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting changed the paradigm of trade theory and empirics after the new trade theory. The framework gave a new channel for gains from trade and became the basis of quantitative trade work.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central paper. Helpman, with Melitz and Yeaple, supplied the key extension to the exporting-versus-FDI choice. Redding's quantitative and spatial contributions are important, but the main discovery was made earlier. Helpman also appears under B039 and would offer broad prior contributions, but this ballot should be assessed on its own.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of use and extensive empirical validation of the main implications. The award timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Krugman received the 2008 prize for trade theory and economic geography, so there is some overlap
Judging Redding against Helpman for the third place
Quantitative welfare gains depend on model assumptions

assessment.nobel_worthiness: These authors built the modern economic analysis of political institutions. They combined theory and empirics on electoral rules, constitutions, fiscal policy and state capacity, and they bridged political science and economics. The 2024 prize overlapped on institutions, but this body of work has distinct content.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini jointly produced the core framework, summarised in their 2000 book and constitutional-effects papers. Besley's contributions on state capacity and accountability are closely connected, so the trio is coherent.
assessment.maturity: Developed from the 1990s onward with empirical support in cross-country and subnational data. It is mature.
uncertainties: Identification in cross-country constitutional comparisons is difficult
Overlap with the 2024 prize on institutions
Whether a political-economy award is seen as a priority now

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework and the monetary policy rule literature are the working basis of central-bank analysis worldwide. Both the theory and the policy impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: The credit is highly dispersed across eight listed names, including Calvo, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Gertler and Smets. Woodford gave the theoretical foundation, Taylor the policy rule, and Gali the estimation and clarification of the framework. Any three leave out others with strong claims, and some of these contributors are also credited elsewhere on the list.
assessment.maturity: Developed over thirty years and well tested through practice. It is mature.
uncertainties: A very difficult attribution problem with many deserving contributors
Lucas, Sargent, Sims, Kydland and Prescott, and Phelps already cover adjacent macro territory
The framework's performance after 2008 and after the 2021-22 inflation has been questioned

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run top-income and wealth data series changed the empirical basis of the inequality debate, and the work also affected tax policy research. The measurement achievement is substantial, and the data are now an international infrastructure.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez built the top-income series, and Zucman contributed the wealth and offshore-wealth estimates. The contributions are clear, but the interpretive and theoretical claims of some of the work are more contested than the data work.
assessment.maturity: The income-series work dates from the early 2000s and is well established. The wealth and offshore estimates are more recent and still debated.
uncertainties: Methodological disputes about wealth and income imputations
Whether the committee views the contribution as measurement or as analysis
Zucman's work is relatively recent, which makes a three-name award harder to justify
